# ezghcloud_cache_user (Resource)

A user of a cache. Its password is generated and kept in a Secret in the cache's project; Terraform state never holds it. Destroying it deletes the user and its Secret. The user default comes with the cache and can't be destroyed.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cache_id` (String) Cache (cch_) it belongs to. Changing it replaces the user.
- `name` (String) Username: a lowercase letter, then up to 31 lowercase letters, digits, _ and -. ezgh_ names are reserved. Changing it replaces the user.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cache. Changing it replaces the user.

### Optional

- `preset` (String) Valkey only: readWrite or readOnly (readWrite when left out at create; removing it later keeps the current preset). Changes in place. Null on Memcached, whose users have full access.

### Read-Only

- `failure_code` (String) Why the user's last operation failed, as a code; null when it didn't.
- `failure_message` (String) Why the user's last operation failed; null when it didn't.
- `id` (String) cache_id/name.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `secret_id` (String) The Secret (sec_) holding the user's username, password, host, port, engine and, on Valkey, a rediss:// uri.
- `status` (String) What the user is doing: creating, available, modifying, rotating, deleting or failed.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_cache_user.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CACHE_ID/NAME'
```
